Generate, Score, & Implement Elite Prompts The Opik Agent Optimizer SDK comes with everything you need to generate new prompts automatically, score them based on your eval criteria, and trust that the best version makes it to production. Run Seven Prompt Optimization Algorithms in One Package Few-Shot Bayesian Optimizer Ideal for text-based chat models with template-based, stable examples Automatically finds the best set of few-shot example combinations Efficient, probabilistic framework chooses which combination to try next View Docs Hierarchical Reflective Prompt Optimizer (HRPO) Identifies failed outcomes from existing prompts and applies hierarchical root-cause analysis Generates targeted improvements to systematically address each failure mode Ideal when you have a complex prompt that needs to be surgically fixed rather than entirely rewritten View Docs MetaPrompt Optimizer Refines and expands your initial prompt draft using a reasoning model Improves wording, structure, and clarity to achieve better results that more closely resemble your golden dataset Iteratively generates and scores multiple prompt candidates and returns the best one View Docs Evolutionary Optimizer Optimizes for multiple objectives and adds diversity and exploration to your workflow Uses genetic algorithms with selection, mutation, and crossover operations Stronger ability to “think outside the box” and discover new prompt solutions View Docs GEPA Optimizer Wraps the external GEPA package to optimize a single system prompt for single-turn tasks Optimizes using a task model and a reflection model to return optimized results Expands GEPA’s built-in baseline evaluation with the full suite of Opik LLM evaluation metrics for more precise optimization View Docs Parameter Optimizer Finds the best parameter or configuration for your specific task when you already have a solid prompt Uses Bayesian optimization to tune LLM call parameters like temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, and more Tunes model behavior without interfering with your actual prompt text View Docs Tool Optimization (MCP & Function Calling) Extends prompt optimization capabilities to prompts that use external tools and function calls like MCP (Model Context Protocol), tool schemas with structured definitions and parameters, and multi-step agentic workflows True tool optimization means Opik can optimize the tools themselves, their schemas, or MCP integrations, where other algorithms simply optimize agents that use tools Ideal for modern agentic systems that require integration with external APIs and services, structured data processing through function calls, complex multi-step reasoning with tools, or dynamic tool selection based on context View Docs Opik is Free & Fully Open Source LLM observability should be accessible to everyone building the next generation of AI applications and agents. Getting Started Quickstart Ask a question | Copy page | View as Markdown | More actions This guide helps you integrate the Opik platform with your existing Agent. The goal of this guide is to help you log your first traces and start tracking your prompts and agent configuration in Opik. Prerequisites Before you begin, you’ll need to choose how you want to use Opik: Opik Cloud : Create a free account at comet.com/opik Self-hosting : Follow the self-hosting guide to deploy Opik locally or on Kubernetes Logging your first LLM calls Opik makes it easy to integrate with your existing LLM application. Pick the tab that matches your stack and follow the three steps to log your first trace: Python SDK TypeScript SDK OpenAI (Python) OpenAI (TS) LangGraph AI integration All integrations If you are using the Python function decorator, you can integrate by: 1 Install the Opik Python SDK: pip install opik 2 Configure the Opik Python SDK: opik configure 3 Wrap your function with the @track decorator: from opik import track @ track def my_function ( input : str ) -> str : return input All calls to the my_function will now be logged to Opik. This works well for any function even nested ones and is also supported by most integrations (just wrap any parent function with the @track decorator). Analyze your traces After running your application, you will start seeing your traces in Opik and you can use Ollie to analyze them and improve your agent. If you don’t see traces appearing, reach out to us on Slack or raise an issue on GitHub and we’ll help you troubleshoot. Recommended if you build with an AI coding assistant. Connect your assistant (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more) to Opik and it can read these traces, score outputs and run evaluations from chat, keeping observability where you are already working. One command, uvx opik mcp configure , installs both the MCP server and the Opik skills and needs no SDK; see MCP server . Next steps Now that you have logged your first traces, here’s what to explore next: In depth guide on agent observability : Learn how to customize the data that is logged to Opik and how to log conversations.
